:::{#exm-divergent-sequence}
#### A divergent sequence

$c_n = n$ diverges.
For any real number $L$ and $\tolout = 1$,
every $n > L + 1$ has $\abs{n - L} > 1$,
so no $N$ works.
For example, with $L = 5$, every $n \ge 7$ has $\abs{n - 5} \ge 2$.
It diverges to $\infty$:
for every real number $M$, every $n \ge N$ has $c_n = n > M$
when $N$ is a natural number larger than $M$.

:::
